predictions.selection_reason: Handler object -> hasOwnProperty check -> prevents prototype pollution
predictions.source_summary: The 'name' variable comes from this.fn.toString(options), where 'fn' is the function name part of a FunctionNode. The 'options' parameter is passed to the toString method and may contain user-provided configuration.
predictions.sink_summary: The property access options.handler[name] is used to call a custom handler function: options.handler[name](this, options). This could potentially lead to code execution if attacker controls the handler object and property name.
predictions.guard_summary: The hasOwnProperty check prevents prototype pollution by ensuring the property exists directly on the handler object, not inherited from Object.prototype. The check also validates that options.handler is an object before accessing it.
predictions.risk_pattern: Safe property access check added to prevent prototype pollution when accessing custom handler functions in the toString method. The check ensures that only properties directly defined on the handler object are accessed, preventing inheritance chain attacks.
predictions.context_summary: The change adds a prototype pollution protection check in FunctionNode's toString method when accessing custom handler functions. This prevents attackers from polluting Object.prototype to inject malicious handlers.
unresolved_facts: Exact implementation of this.fn.toString() to determine what values 'name' can contain
How the options parameter flows into this function and whether it can be attacker-controlled
Whether there are other paths to prototype pollution in the codebase
